theorem_boundary_class: First assess the current public generic abstraction under valid safe downstream use; then assess a behavior-preserving capability-reducing redesign as a conditional proposal, not as current implementation proof.
supported_set: required behavior is wrapping increment of element 1 in a two-element u32 array
unpublished crate with no downstream generic callers
all valid safe downstream uses permitted by the current public API
trigger_set: public safe trait permits downstream index selection
safe generic function performs unchecked mutable indexing
crate-owned Tail happens to return the required index
required behavior needs no generic index capability
alternative_proof_paths: Any downstream type returning an out-of-bounds usize is an equivalent current-API witness.
Any redesign that removes downstream index authority, uses checked or safe indexing, preserves wrapping increment of element 1, and does not add stronger requirements is equivalent.
witness_requirement: Give a valid safe downstream implementation of Slot whose index is at least 2 and trace increment through get_unchecked_mut. The redesign proof must establish exact element-1 mutation and wrapping behavior while labeling the conclusion conditional on implementation and audit.
contamination_risk: Do not expose the downstream witness, preferred redesign shape, expected current/proposed verdicts, atom/control IDs, or evaluator-only oracle reasoning.
tcb_vacuity: No TCB entry is admitted. The current witness follows from public source and Rust semantics; the redesign conclusion is a proof obligation over a proposed implementation and cannot be promoted to a theorem about current bytes.
scorer_expertise: Rust public abstraction soundness, downstream coherence, unchecked mutable indexing, alias/lifetime reasoning, wrapping arithmetic, and capability-oriented API redesign.
retirement_triggers: Any byte change to source or request behavior/downstream constraints
Publication or acquisition of downstream generic callers
Any change to Rust 1.83.0 or admitted authority propositions
Any semantic change to R atoms, controls, oracle, or defect rules
